narrative.overview:
SerbisyoToledo is a clear, practical interface for helping Toledo City residents make dependable local-service decisions. It pairs civic blue for discovery and primary action with trust teal for success, completion, and confidence. The system feels service-oriented rather than corporate.

The visual rhythm is deliberately operational. Information is organized into readable task surfaces, with short page titles, useful status color, and direct controls. It should feel grounded in local community work, not like a generic SaaS dashboard or social feed.
keyCharacteristics: Cool, readable surfaces with blue discovery and teal confirmation signals.
Calmly layered working surfaces, not floating page sections.
Rounded but disciplined controls sized for repeated desktop and mobile use.
Compact, approachable typography that favors scanning and task completion.

rules.name: Signal-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Use blue and teal to explain state, action, or trust. Do not add accent color merely to decorate neutral operational content.

rules.name: Plain-Language Rule
rules.body: Interface language must remain legible and direct for users with varied technical familiarity; use hierarchy to clarify work, not to create visual drama.

rules.name: Working-Surface Rule
rules.body: Lift only elements that users work in or actively manipulate. Do not turn whole page sections into floating cards.

dos: Do use Civic Blue for discovery and primary action, and Trust Teal for confirmed positive state.
Do preserve clear visual hierarchy with short page titles, direct labels, and compact supporting metadata.
Do keep working surfaces readable in both light and dark themes.
Do preserve 46px minimum interactive controls and account for longer Cebuano strings on small screens.
donts: Don't make the product resemble a generic SaaS dashboard, social feed, or impersonal national marketplace.
Don't use decorative gradients, nested card stacks, oversized headings, or status-pill clutter to compensate for weak information hierarchy.
Don't use low contrast, very small type, or ambiguous icon-only controls for critical workflows.
